chapters.title: Chapter 1: Why These Three Documents Matter

lessons.title: The Income-tax Act, 2025: The Tax Year and What Changes for These Forms

children.text: If you filed your return this July, you used Form 16, Form 26AS and AIS exactly as the last two lessons described. The documents you receive next year will carry different names. On 1 April 2026, India replaced a tax law that had been in force since 1962 with a new one. The reporting trail works the same way, but the vocabulary has changed, and some of the new terms are easy to misread.
A New Law, Not a New Tax

The Income-tax Act, 2025 received Presidential assent on 21 August 2025 and came into force on 1 April 2026, replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961. The Income-tax Rules, 2026, notified in March 2026, replaced the Income-tax Rules, 1962. Those Rules are where the forms live, so they are the reason your certificates get new numbers.

The aim of the rewrite was structure and plain language. Decades of amendments had left the 1961 Act full of sections such as 194BA and 80CCD(1B). The new Act regroups provisions and uses tables in many places. For example, the entire 194 series of TDS provisions now sits under one section, 393.

body.text: Throughout this course, we cite the Income-tax Act, 2025 section first and give the familiar 1961 Act section in brackets, for example section 392 (section 192). That way you can follow both current documents and older articles.

children.text: The Tax Year Replaces Two Confusing Terms
Under the 1961 Act, every year had two labels. The
previous year
was the year you earned income. The
assessment year
was the following year, when that income was assessed. Income earned from April 2025 to March 2026 belonged to previous year 2025-26 and assessment year 2026-27.

markDefs.definition: Under the 1961 Act, the financial year in which income was earned, running 1 April to 31 March.
Under the 1961 Act, the year after the previous year, in which that income was assessed and the return filed.

children.text: The new Act drops both labels and uses a single term, the
tax year
. The tax year is simply the financial year in which you earn the income.

markDefs.definition: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the 12-month period from 1 April to 31 March in which income is earned. It replaces both previous year and assessment year.

body.label: Tax year 2026-27
body.context: The first tax year under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Its return is filed in 2027.

body.caption: Same income period, old and new labels

body.text: AY 2026-27 and tax year 2026-27 are not the same year. AY 2026-27 means income earned in FY 2025-26, filed in 2026. Tax year 2026-27 means income earned from April 2026, filed in 2027. When a document, notice or article mentions 2026-27, check which label it uses before you act on it.

children.text: The Switchover, Step by Step

body.title: From the 1961 Act to the 2025 Act

events.title: Presidential assent
events.description: The Income-tax Act, 2025 is enacted, to take effect from 1 April 2026.

events.title: Income-tax Rules, 2026 notified
events.description: The new Rules prescribe the renumbered forms, including Forms 130, 138 and 168.

events.title: New Act in force
events.description: Tax year 2026-27 begins. TDS deducted from April 2026 salary falls under section 392.

events.title: Last Form 16 under the old law
events.description: Employers issue Form 16 for FY 2025-26, because that income was earned under the 1961 Act.

events.title: Two systems side by side
events.description: Returns for FY 2025-26 are due under the 1961 Act, while employers file the first quarterly salary TDS statements in the new Form 138 for April to June 2026.

events.title: First Form 130
events.description: Employers issue the new salary TDS certificate for tax year 2026-27.

events.title: First return under the new Act
events.description: You file your return for tax year 2026-27, checking it against Form 130 and Form 168.

children.text: The Forms You Will Actually See
The Rules renumbered hundreds of forms, but only a handful touch a salaried taxpayer or small investor directly:

body.caption: Old and new form numbers that matter for this course

cells: TDS certificate for other payments, such as FD interest
Statement of perquisites from your employer
Your declaration of HRA, deductions and investments to HR
Declaration for no TDS on interest (non-senior and senior)
Quarterly TDS statement for other payments

children.text: Form 130: Form 16 With a Different Layout

Form 130 is issued under section 395 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 203 of the 1961 Act) and is due by 15 June after the end of the tax year, the same deadline as Form 16. The biggest visible change is the layout. Form 16 had two parts. Form 130 is organised as follows:
Part A:
Details of the certificate, the employer and the employee.
Part B:
A summary of salary paid and TDS deducted each quarter, with details of how the tax was deposited.
Annexures:
The salary computation, covering gross salary, exemptions, deductions, taxable income and tax, with a separate annexure for pension and interest of specified senior citizens.
The guidance note on Form 130 says the certificate is valid only if it is generated from the TRACES portal and signed by the deductor. It also uses tax year in place of assessment year.
Form 168: Form 26AS and AIS in One Statement

Form 168 is the annual information statement under section 510 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 285BB of the 1961 Act). Instead of checking a narrow tax credit statement in one place and a wider information statement in another, you get one statement. Part A holds your identity details. Part B holds TDS and TCS entries, SFT information from banks, registrars and brokers, advance and self-assessment tax, refunds and demands.
The Taxpayer Information Summary and the option to give feedback on wrong entries continue, so the checks you learn in Chapters 3 and 4 still apply.

body.title: What changes and what stays the same

columns.label: What changes
points: Form numbers, such as Form 16 becoming Form 130
Previous year and assessment year become tax year
Form 26AS and AIS are presented together as Form 168

columns.label: What stays the same
points: Employers, banks and registrars still report against your PAN
Quarterly TDS statements and their due dates
The 15 June deadline for your salary TDS certificate
TIS and the AIS feedback facility
The need to reconcile everything before you file

body.text: New names, same trail. If you can reconcile Form 16 with Form 26AS and AIS, you can reconcile Form 130 with Form 168.

children.text: Which Rules Apply to You Right Now?

The test is simple: look at when the income was earned. Income earned up to 31 March 2026 is dealt with under the 1961 Act, with its old forms, even if you file, revise or receive a notice about it later. Income earned from 1 April 2026 onward falls under the Income-tax Act, 2025.

This course teaches the documents in the order you will meet them. Chapters 2 to 4 use Form 16, Form 26AS and AIS, because those are the documents for the returns most readers are dealing with today, and each lesson flags what changes under Form 130 and Form 168.
Check Your Understanding

body.title: Decode the year
body.question: Meera receives a document referring to "AY 2026-27". Which income does it relate to?
options: Income earned from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027
Income earned from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026
Income earned from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028
It is the same as tax year 2026-27
body.explanation: Assessment year 2026-27 is the year after previous year 2025-26, so it covers income earned in FY 2025-26. Tax year 2026-27 is a different period: April 2026 to March 2027.

body.title: The new salary certificate
body.textWithBlank: For salary earned in tax year 2026-27, your employer will issue Form ___ instead of Form 16.
body.explanation: Form 130 replaces Form 16 under the Income-tax Rules, 2026. It is due by 15 June 2027 for tax year 2026-27.

body.title: Karan reads a scary headline
body.scenario: In September 2026, Karan, a bank employee in Kolkata, sees a social media post saying "Form 16 abolished, new Income Tax Act in force". He filed his return for FY 2025-26 in July using the Form 16 his employer issued in June 2026. He now worries his return is invalid and that he must refile using Form 130.
body.prompt: Is Karan right to worry? What should he understand about which law and forms apply?
body.modelAnswer: No. His salary was earned from April 2025 to March 2026, before the new Act took effect, so it is dealt with under the 1961 Act. Form 16 was the correct certificate for that income and his return does not need refiling because of the change in law. Form 130 applies to salary earned from 1 April 2026 onward, so the first one he receives will be for tax year 2026-27, by 15 June 2027. What Karan should do now is keep his FY 2025-26 documents safely, and expect new form names next year.

cards.definition: Now Form 130. Salary TDS certificate from your employer, due by 15 June after the tax year.
Now Form 131. TDS certificate for payments other than salary, such as FD interest.
Now Form 124. Your statement to HR of claims such as HRA, home loan interest and deductions.
Now Form 123. Your employer's statement of perquisites, such as a company car or ESOPs.
Now Form 121. Declaration asking a bank not to deduct TDS when your income is below the taxable limit.
Now Form 168. One annual statement of TDS, TCS, SFT information, taxes paid, refunds and demands.
Now Form 138. The employer's quarterly salary TDS statement.
Now tax year. The 1 April to 31 March period in which income is earned.

points: The Income-tax Act, 2025 and Income-tax Rules, 2026 replaced the 1961 Act and 1962 Rules from 1 April 2026.
Tax year replaces previous year and assessment year. Tax year 2026-27 runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.
AY 2026-27 and tax year 2026-27 are different periods, so always check which label a document uses.
Income earned up to 31 March 2026 stays under the 1961 Act and its forms, including Form 16 and Form 26AS.
From tax year 2026-27, Form 16 becomes Form 130 and Form 26AS and AIS come together as Form 168.
The reporting trail, the quarterly TDS cycle and the 15 June certificate deadline do not change.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and reflects the law and CBDT guidance available as of September 2026. Form layouts and portal features under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 may be refined through further notifications. For your specific situation, check the e-filing portal or consult a chartered accountant.
